summary.intent: Start a new GSD milestone (v2.0 Metadata and Sharing Refactor) for CipherBox, covering the full new-milestone workflow: project context update, optional research, requirements definition, and roadmap creation.
summary.outcome: Completed all workflow gates: PROJECT.md and STATE.md updated for v2.0, Architecture + Pitfalls research completed and synthesized, 39 requirements defined across 8 categories in REQUIREMENTS.md, and a 9-phase roadmap (phases 61–69) created and committed on branch docs/v2.0-metadata-and-sharing-refactor.

repo: Main branch is protected from direct commits; planning docs must go through feature branches following the docs/<name> naming convention
Signing commits requires unsandboxed access to the 1Password agent (--gpg-sign fails in sandbox)
.planning/research/ is gitignored — stale content from prior milestones persists untracked and must be archived manually before new milestone research
v1.1 ended at phase 60; v2.0 continues numbering at phase 61 (phase numbering is continuous across milestones unless --reset-phase-numbers is passed)
v1.1 had no REQUIREMENTS.md on disk — the file was created fresh for v2.0
The repo has a milestone_branch_template in config that informs branch naming

gsd_run query agent-skills returns empty output for gsd-project-researcher, gsd-research-synthesizer, gsd-roadmapper — agent skills are self-contained in the subagent prompts, not injected via the CLI

code.finding: Implementation-ready design with ratified ADRs, a frozen cutover order (§7.2), and a 21-item must-pass-before-merge test strategy (§7.3); three open questions remain in §9.2 (co-writer offline, rotation host for pure-web users, write-recipient authority)

9-phase roadmap (61–69) follows strict dependency chain: crypto → core → sdk-core → sdk → api → tee → web → fuse; roadmapper independently verified 39/39 requirements mapped, correcting an earlier count of 36
39 requirements across CRYPTO, NODE, READ, ROT, WRITE, TEE, DATA, TEST categories; Tier 3 (capability layer / read-side TTL) and SEED-001 explicitly deferred to Future Requirements

workflow: The gsd commit helper fails silently when on a protected branch — files stay staged, no error is surfaced, no commit is created; direct git commit is required
The synthesizer subagent can be blocked from writing files by sandbox permissions; when this happens the orchestrator must write SUMMARY.md manually from the returned content
For implementation-ready designs with ratified ADRs, skip open-ended questioning and go straight to scope confirmation — the design document is the source of truth
Archiving stale research files before spawning new researchers prevents confusion about which outputs are current; the archive step is not part of the workflow spec but is necessary in practice
When only a subset of researchers are needed (Architecture + Pitfalls, not Stack + Features), the synthesizer prompt must be adjusted to reference only the files that were actually written

friction: gsd commit helper silently no-ops on a protected main branch — left files staged with no error, required discovery via git log before switching to direct git
Commit signing requires unsandboxed 1Password agent access; every git commit needed the user to approve the sandboxed tool call or use a workaround
gsd_run query agent-skills returned empty output for all three GSD agent types — had to proceed without injected skills context
Synthesizer subagent was blocked from writing SUMMARY.md to disk; orchestrator had to write the file manually from the returned text
Stale v1.1 research files (SUMMARY.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, PITFALLS.md, m4/ dir, questions.md) were sitting in .planning/research/ and needed manual archiving before v2.0 research could begin
Miscounted requirements during definition (reported 36, actual count was 39 across 8 categories = 3+6+5+7+4+7+4+3); the roadmapper caught and corrected this
open_items: §9.2 Q1: Co-writer offline handling during rotation — pinned to Phase 63/68
§9.2 Q2: Rotation host for pure-web users (no desktop/FUSE) — pinned to Phase 63
§9.2 Q3: Write-recipient vs owner authority for sub-shares — pinned to Phase 65/68
Phase 66 research flag: TypeORM FK map for share_keys → shares migration
Phase 69 research flag: grant-root algorithm for FUSE re-encryption callers
SEED-001 (Phala TEE on-demand cost reduction) deferred to future milestone
Tier 3 (capability layer / read-side TTL cache) explicitly out of scope for v2.0
